label: rem:observability-fluid-context
title: Observability for the brane fluid
html:
Before formalising NS regularity, we clarify the QOU observability axiom \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 structurally within the fluid-dynamical setting.

Categorical statement. No morphism \phi \colon \mathbf{1} \to \mathrm{Ad}(A) exists within \mathbf{C}. The adjoint representation of the Frobenius--Hopf object A admits no trivial sub-object.

Gauge-theoretic translation. H^0(M, \mathrm{Ad}(P)) = 0: no nonzero section of the adjoint bundle \mathrm{Ad}(P) = P \times_G \mathfrak{g} remains gauge-equivariant. Every infinitesimal gauge transformation operates nontrivially against some observable.

Contact-geometric translation. The Levi form \mathcal{L}_\varTheta operates non-degenerately everywhere. The horizontal distribution \ker(\varTheta) stays maximally non-integrable (forbidding integral submanifolds of dimension > \frac{1}{2}\dim\ker\varTheta).

Fluid-dynamical translation. Evaluated on the brane fluid:

  1. No stagnant directions. Every spatial direction in the brane actively drives fluid dynamics. The gauge structure strictly forbids directions supporting an identically zero velocity field.
  2. Vortex cores are tubular. The core-Levi equivalence ensures that non-degenerate Levi form caps the core aspect ratio. The core cannot flatten out into a sheet or compress into a one-dimensional needle.
  3. No hidden laminar sectors. If \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) \neq 0, a gauge symmetry would render a designated direction dynamically trivial, yielding a guaranteed laminar sector. Observability precludes this: every direction forces dynamic engagement.
  4. Vortex stretching is isotropic. The weight-space decomposition of the adjoint bundle lacks a trivial component. Consequently, the stretching term (\omega \cdot \nabla)v applies pressure in all directions. Vorticity cannot vent into a "neutral" axis.

The alternative: what \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) \neq 0 implies.

A surviving morphism \phi \colon \mathbf{1} \to \mathrm{Ad}(A) would establish a preferred direction operating in the brane:

  • A 1-dimensional foliation embedded in the contact distribution (establishing partial integrability).
  • A designated axis where vortex stretching zeroes out.
  • A physical channel permitting vorticity to drain without local concentration.
  • A structural mechanism enabling vortex cores to unroll into sheets.

This structural leak would provide a persistent regularity mechanism: vorticity would dissipate cleanly into the integrable direction rather than concentrating into a blowup.

Observability asserts that no such escape route exists. The brane fluid remains dynamically active; colliding vortices lack any structural geometry to dissipate through.
